snippets.name: email_send
snippets.description: Send an email / e-mail notification / report by mail. Delivers through a configured SMTP relay (Gmail, Microsoft 365, SendGrid, Amazon SES, Mailgun or a custom server — see /email). Use this whenever a workflow should email someone. Set `to` and `subject` in the node's config_overrides plus `body` (plain text) and/or `html`; optional `cc`, `bcc`, `reply_to` and `attachments` (base64 — feed it from an upstream `report` step). Omit `channel_id` to use the default channel. Host, port, TLS and the password live on the channel, never on the node. The send is NOT reversible. Branch on {{ steps.X.output.ok }}. Use target_mode='once' (not device-scoped).

cc.description: Optional carbon-copy recipient(s), same shape as `to`.

to.description: Recipient(s): one address, a comma-separated string, or an array of addresses.

bcc.description: Optional blind-copy recipient(s), same shape as `to`.

body.description: Plain-text body. Supply `body`, `html`, or both — at least one is required.

html.description: HTML body. When supplied alone, a plain-text alternative is generated automatically.

subject.description: Subject line. Templates like {{ steps.X.output.field }} expand before send.

from_name.description: Optional display name for the sender.

channel_id.description: Optional. The EmailChannel (SMTP relay) to send through — a UUID from /email. Omit to use the deployment's default channel.

attachments.description: Optional attachments. Feed content_base64 from an upstream `report` step to email a generated PDF/XLSX.

from_address.description: Optional override of the channel's sender. Most providers reject a From they do not own.

ok.description: TRUE only when the SMTP server accepted the message — branch on this.

error.description: SMTP failure reason when ok=false (auth rejected, TLS handshake, unreachable relay).

provider.description: gmail | outlook365 | sendgrid | ses | mailgun | smtp.

message_id.description: RFC 5322 Message-ID of the sent message.

snippets.name: dns-reconcile-infoblox-csv-once
snippets.description: Reconcile active NetBox devices against Infoblox host records, classify DNS status, and build a timestamped CSV payload for email/reporting.
snippets.code:
import csv
import io
import base64
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from flowweaver_runtime import get_input, set_output, integration


def _strip_cidr(value):
    if not value:
        return ""
    return str(value).split("/")[0]


def _normalize_tags(tags):
    out = []
    for t in tags or []:
        if isinstance(t, dict):
            slug = t.get("slug") or t.get("name")
            if slug:
                out.append(str(slug))
        elif isinstance(t, str):
            out.append(t)
    return out


inp = get_input()
nb = inp["steps"]["fetch-netbox-devices"]["output"]
if "data" not in nb or "results" not in nb["data"]:
    raise ValueError(f"expected NetBox list response under output.data.results, got keys: {sorted(nb)}")

devices = nb["data"]["results"]
infoblox = integration("infoblox")
rows = []
updates = []
timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")

for dev in devices:
    name = str(dev.get("name") or "").strip()
    primary = dev.get("primary_ip4") or {}
    ip = _strip_cidr(primary.get("address"))
    if not name:
        continue

    existing_tags = _normalize_tags(dev.get("tags"))

    search = infoblox.get("/record:host", params={"name": name})
    if not search.ok:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Infoblox lookup failed for device '{name}': HTTP {search.status_code} - {search.text[:300]}"
        )
    try:
        payload = search.json()
    except Exception as err:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Infoblox returned invalid JSON for device '{name}' (HTTP {search.status_code}): {err}"
        )

    # Only an explicit, successfully-parsed empty list means "no DNS record".
    # A non-list payload is not a shape Infoblox's /record:host is documented
    # to return on success, so treat it as an error rather than guessing.
    if not isinstance(payload, list):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Infoblox returned an unexpected payload shape for device '{name}' "
            f"(HTTP {search.status_code}): expected a JSON list, got {type(payload).__name__}"
        )

    exists = bool(payload)
    status = "In Sync" if exists else "Missing DNS"
    tag = "dns-verified" if exists else "missing-dns"

    rows.append([name, ip, status, tag])
    updates.append({
        "device_id": dev.get("id"),
        "device_name": name,
        "ip": ip,
        "status": status,
        "tag": tag,
        "existing_tags": existing_tags,
    })

buf = io.StringIO()
writer = csv.writer(buf)
writer.writerow(["device_name", "ip", "status", "tag"])
writer.writerows(rows)
content = buf.getvalue().encode("utf-8")

set_output({
    "timestamp": timestamp,
    "filename": f"dns-inventory-reconciliation-{timestamp}.csv",
    "content_type": "text/csv",
    "content_base64": base64.b64encode(content).decode("ascii"),
    "row_count": len(rows),
    "rows": rows,
    "updates": updates,
})
snippets.logic_diagram_mermaid:
flowchart TD
    in([Input: NetBox device list + Infoblox integration]) --> loop{For each device}
    loop --> host[Extract name, primary IP, existing tags]
    host --> lookup[Infoblox GET /record:host?name=device]
    lookup --> okcheck{HTTP ok?}
    okcheck -->|no| fail1([step FAILS: names device + HTTP status])
    okcheck -->|yes| parse{Valid JSON list?}
    parse -->|no / wrong shape| fail2([step FAILS: names device + HTTP status])
    parse -->|yes, non-empty| sync[Status = In Sync / Tag = dns-verified]
    parse -->|yes, empty| miss[Status = Missing DNS / Tag = missing-dns]
    sync --> row[Append CSV row + update payload]
    miss --> row
    row --> loop
    loop -->|done| csv[Build timestamped CSV]
    csv --> out([Output: filename, content_base64, rows, updates])

snippets.name: apply-netbox-dns-tags-once
snippets.description: Apply reconciliation tags back to NetBox while preserving existing tags.
snippets.code:
from flowweaver_runtime import get_input, set_output, integration


# Mutually exclusive DNS reconciliation tags: applying one must remove the other.
OPPOSITE_TAG = {
    "dns-verified": "missing-dns",
    "missing-dns": "dns-verified",
}


def _normalize_tags(tags):
    slugs = []
    for t in tags or []:
        if isinstance(t, dict):
            slug = t.get("slug") or t.get("name")
            if slug and slug not in slugs:
                slugs.append(str(slug))
        elif isinstance(t, str):
            if t not in slugs:
                slugs.append(t)
    return slugs


def _reconciled_tags(existing, new_slug):
    """Add new_slug, drop its opposite DNS tag, keep every other tag as-is."""
    slugs = _normalize_tags(existing)
    opposite = OPPOSITE_TAG.get(new_slug)
    result = [s for s in slugs if s != opposite]
    if new_slug not in result:
        result.append(new_slug)
    return result


inp = get_input()
reconcile = inp["steps"]["reconcile-dns"]["output"]
if "updates" not in reconcile:
    raise ValueError(f"expected reconcile output.updates, got keys: {sorted(reconcile)}")

nb = integration("netbox")
results = []
updated_count = 0
skipped_count = 0
unchanged_count = 0

for item in reconcile["updates"]:
    device_id = item.get("device_id")
    if not device_id:
        skipped_count += 1
        results.append({"device_name": item.get("device_name"), "ok": False, "reason": "missing device_id"})
        continue

    existing_slugs = _normalize_tags(item.get("existing_tags"))
    new_slugs = _reconciled_tags(item.get("existing_tags"), item.get("tag"))

    # Order-independent comparison: same set of tags means nothing to PATCH.
    if set(new_slugs) == set(existing_slugs):
        unchanged_count += 1
        results.append({
            "device_id": device_id,
            "device_name": item.get("device_name"),
            "tag": item.get("tag"),
            "ok": True,
            "changed": False,
            "reason": "tags already correct, PATCH skipped",
        })
        continue

    tags = [{"slug": s} for s in new_slugs]
    resp = nb.patch(f"/api/dcim/devices/{device_id}/", json={"tags": tags})
    ok = bool(resp.ok)
    if ok:
        updated_count += 1
    else:
        skipped_count += 1

    results.append({
        "device_id": device_id,
        "device_name": item.get("device_name"),
        "tag": item.get("tag"),
        "ok": ok,
        "changed": ok,
        "status_code": resp.status_code,
        "error": None if ok else resp.text[:300],
    })

set_output({
    "updated_count": updated_count,
    "skipped_count": skipped_count,
    "unchanged_count": unchanged_count,
    "results": results,
})
snippets.logic_diagram_mermaid:
flowchart TD
    in([Input: reconcile updates + NetBox integration]) --> client[Resolve NetBox client via integration("netbox")]
    client --> loop{For each device update}
    loop --> norm[Normalize existing tags]
    norm --> compute[Add target tag, remove opposite DNS tag, keep all others]
    compute --> same{New tag set == existing tag set?}
    same -->|yes| skip[Skip PATCH, count unchanged]
    same -->|no| patch[PATCH NetBox device tags]
    patch --> ok{Patch succeeded?}
    ok -->|yes| good[Count updated]
    ok -->|no| bad[Count skipped + capture error]
    skip --> loop
    good --> loop
    bad --> loop
    loop -->|done| out([Output: updated_count, skipped_count, unchanged_count, results])
